definitions_and_limits: All 24 attempts are included. Completion claims means the final candidate response. Intermediate factual errors are retained separately and do not silently change the preregistered completion gate.

Before first try counts native PHP Read calls before the first rename invocation, including one that fails. Before successful write includes recovery Reads after a refused invocation. Native Reads are counted individually, not as unique files.
Source-read counts cover recognized native Read calls. Bash Git diffs are retained separately and can also expose source. No shell commands or candidate code were run for this audit.

Control run024 reads both warned files with two Bash grep calls, not native Read. Those calls are included in the separately labeled combined warned-file source-call total; native Read counts retain their original tool-specific meaning.

A read of a file named in an engine warning is observed, not automatically proof that every warning was reviewed. Warning review and explicit user preservation requirements can justify post-write Reads. The counters do not claim all such Reads are removable.

Repeated checks are explicit php check.php calls after the engine already reported the identical project check passed, with no intervening candidate mutation. Other source review and the independent expected-change oracle remain distinct: the cross-file runtime check also accepts the old method via its fallback.

The only PHP writes visible in these traces are the engine invocations. Reported before/after hashes match retained fixture hashes, and reported changed files equal the final changed-file set. This is evidence for these attempts, not a universal security claim.

Output includes deterministic printer whitespace: Product.php gains a final newline; the four changed cross-file PHP files lose one trailing blank line. Protected fixtures and unrelated files remain unchanged.

Both arms receive the same already-selected metadata and complete command, and use the same engine and snapshot/excerpt computation. Only review_excerpts presents additive before-command source context; this tests report presentation, not autonomous discovery or an AST-versus-text advantage.

All physical intervention checks passed against native completed evidence. Location-only output is byte-identical to original stdout. Excerpt output preserves original report bytes/values and all supplied source lines/hashes match the before-command fixtures. Full excerpts remain in immutable native/evidence records rather than being duplicated here.

Warned-file Read counts mean file paths named by the original report, not proof of semantic review. A complete single-line excerpt can still omit adjacent lines of a multiline expression; before-command source does not show the final edited file. Rereading therefore is not automatically redundant.

Tool-execution time, provider cache state and the cost of selecting intent metadata are not inferred by this trace audit. The parent report owns the experimental economic metrics and all-attempt decision.
